title: What Is Cost per Use in Cleaning Operations?
excerpt: Cost per use estimates the chemical or consumable cost of completing one defined cleaning use, dose, task or service event rather than comparing pack prices alone.
seo_title: What Is Cost per Use in Cleaning Operations? | Alle's ClinX
meta_description: Learn how cost per use gives a clearer comparison of cleaning chemicals than pack price alone and what inputs are needed.
content_html:
Cost per use is a practical way to compare cleaning products based on what it costs to complete a defined task or dose. Pack price alone can be misleading when products have different concentrations, dilution rates or dose sizes.

Start with the actual usable quantity

For concentrates, calculate how much ready-to-use solution the pack produces at the approved dilution. For dosing systems, use the actual dose delivered per task.

Define what one use means

One use might be one spray bottle, one bucket, one machine tank, one wash cycle or one standardized cleaning task.

Compare equivalent outcomes

Products should be compared only where they are approved for the same task and provide the required performance and safety controls.

Include avoidable waste where relevant

Over-dosing, discarded solution, product loss or poor dispenser calibration can raise real cost per use above the theoretical value.

Cost per use is not the only decision factor

Safety, compatibility, labour, equipment needs, effectiveness and compliance requirements may be more important than a small unit-cost difference.

Practical takeaway

Use cost per use to compare like-for-like cleaning tasks, not just container prices.
